system.summary: Homophonic alphabet with vowel-consonant syllable signs, word signs, nulls and a dozen code signs (key DECODE R1857 image P11).

prior_solution.where: Late clear copies filed with every copied cipher leaf (Barbavara ff. 39, 48, 55/57, 61, 68, 74; Pusterla ff. 14, 27, 33, 41, 66, 70, 76, 80); 15th-c. decipherment of f. 42 on f. 43; 15th-c. interlinear glosses, in part, on ff. 135 and 143. solution.what: Repo notes and Mazzatinti's ital. 1584 list; lead 1314 points to key DECODE R1857.
Fetched DECODE R1857 metadata and image P11: the key 'Marcolinus de Barbavara et Symon Arrigonus - Petrus de Pusterla' (late copy, some cells blotted).
Mapped Gallica canvases to folios from corner crops; downloaded the full canvases holding every Barbavara cipher leaf.
Leaf-by-leaf check for decipherments: clear copies in a late hand for ff. 40, 49, 56, 62, 69, 75; 15th-c. interlinear glosses on ff. 135, 143.
Spot checks with the R1857 key: f. 69 line 1 = 'in questa hora', f. 40 line 1 = 'se lo c[avalario]', f. 75's clear words recur in order in the f. 74 copy.
Transcribed the six clear copies; noted the copyists' gaps (blank on f. 39, code sign left blank three times on ff. 55v/74v, 'Cologna' for Bologna on f. 68).

ff. 135 and 143: clear text transcribed and the 55 cipher runs deciphered with the R1857 key and the 15th-c. glosses (subagent); 50 read, 5 runs of f. 143 unread (no gloss, blotted key cells); several values rest on the gloss only.
Pusterla's cipher leaves (ff. 13, 32, 42, 67, 71, 77, 81 and the 6 Feb letter) checked: late clear copies for all; f. 43 a 15th-c. decipherment of f. 42.
Pusterla's eight clear copies transcribed and translated (two subagents, checked against the images).

ff. 135 and 143: clear text transcribed and the 55 cipher runs deciphered with the R1857 key and the 15th-c. glosses (subagent); 50 read, 5 runs of f. 143 unread (no gloss, blotted key cells); several values rest on the gloss only.

Code signs the copyist left blank: R1857's label 'Duca di Ferrara' over d+÷ fits all five blanks; d.7 = Veneziani and 9+o = qui (labels fit); the Z-like sign = Micheletto Attendolo [?] from context; the angle sign and four others open.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): (1) the open gap 'Monsignore da Cologna' (copy f. 68) checked on the cipher f. 69 (Gallica canvas 65, l. 2): the cipher has the same word, ott p+ p- ⊃ o- = c-ol-og-n-a, with ott = c, so the slip is in the cipher, not the late copy; gap closed, note in texts/decipherments_18c.md and _en corrected. (2) Independent decoder verify_dudout_20261114.py: the f. 135/143 runs (glossed_runs.tsv) aligned with the deciphered column using only the key values listed in glossed_letters.md and key_R1857_codes.tsv (not the gloss-inferred t-o, h, fto, ϵg, ꝕ): 241 of 495 signs (0.49) fit a key value; only 143.8, 143.25 and 135.2 fit sign for sign, and the runs labelled K (143.24, .26, .48 ...) also need the gloss-inferred values. ʒ= is given an in 143.4 and am in 143.24, 9# ag (key ag = ꝺ#, 9÷o). (3) v10_relabel on the f. 143 section of glossed_letters.md: 0.9496 (641 words, 34 holes) against read_share 0.9 recorded (a run count); still under 0.95, class unchanged. v10 on the whole file gives 0.976 to both f. 135 and f. 143, because both entries point at one file. VERIFY_dudout_20261114.md.

Project check of PR #572 (Brice Dudout): his key-only decoder re-run (241 of 495 signs fit a key-list value; of the runs labelled K only 143.8 and 143.25 fit sign for sign). f. 69 l. 2 looked at on Gallica canvas 65 at full size: a c sign (ott) then p+ p- ⊃ o- after 'da', so Cologna is in the cipher; gap closed. Read share by letter recomputed (v10_relabel.share on the Text sections of glossed_letters.md): f. 135 1.0, f. 143 0.9496 (641 words, 34 holes); read_share of f. 143 set to 0.949 in place of 0.9, which was a run count; still read in part. Page corrected: the Cologna paragraph and the '9 runs from the key alone' line.

outcome.notes: Leads 1313 and 1314 closed 28 Oct 2026. Pusterla folded in from targets/pusterla1447 (one key).

credits.note: Late clear copies of all fourteen copied letters (archive hand, probably 18th c.); 15th-c. decipherment f. 43 and interlinear glosses on ff. 135 and 143.
Identified DECODE R1857 image P11 as the key of BnF ital. 1584 f. 69 (DECODE note, May 2024; cryptiana unsolved.htm).
'Cologna' found in the cipher f. 69 itself (gap closed); key-only decoder of the f. 135/143 runs (241 of 495 signs fit the key list); f. 143 read bar recounted (0.9496)

outcome.method_basis: Every cipher letter of Barbavara and Pusterla in ital. 1584 has a decipherment: a late clear copy filed with it (14 letters) or 15th-century glosses (f. 43; ff. 135 and 143 in part). The work is finding, transcribing and translating them, checking them against the R1857 key, and filling the copyist's blanks for code signs.

texts.label: Pietro Pusterla, Gualdo Tadino, 21 Jan 1447 (cipher f. 13; copy f. 14)

texts.summary: Pusterla tells Sforza he has reached Gualdo and will wait at Montefiascone or Monte Guiduzo for word where to join him, with Antonio da Trezzo, and asks for a guide.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences; coherent throughout; holes only at the copyist's blanks for code signs, most now filled from R1857 and context.

texts.label: Marcolino Barbavara, Rome, undated (late April 1447), f. 135, mostly clear with 4 cipher runs

texts.label: Marcolino Barbavara and Simone Arrigoni, Rome, 4 May 1447, f. 143, mostly clear with 51 cipher runs
texts.summary: The Malatesta coming over to the King, the bulls for their vicariates, the new pope stalling until the outcome is settled, and 4,000 ducats agreed with the Count of Urbino's ambassadors.

reading_review.note: 46 of 51 runs read (9 from the key with the gloss agreeing, 31 key and gloss, 6 gloss alone); runs 143.17, .31, .35, .46, .51 unread: no gloss and blotted key cells.
